newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB CEO SAYS ASIA DEVALUATIONS ALSO OPPORTUNITY.
newsitem.headline: ABB CEO SAYS ASIA DEVALUATIONS ALSO OPPORTUNITY.

text.p: Goran Lindahl, chief executive of ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG, said the recent devaluation of some Asian currencies, particularly the Thai baht, provided an opportunity for ABB by strengthening the competitiveness of its local companies in those countries.

"Of course we prefer a stable and predictable environment and it would have been better if it (the devaluations) had not happened, but we will use it to the best of our ability," Lindahl told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Lindahl said ABB had a policy of hedging its currency exposure so the company would not be hurt by devalutions.
ABB is an extremely decentralised company and emphasises local presence.
Lindahl said the reason for building a local presence was not only to serve local markets, but also to export from these countries.
"With the devaluation of currencies, it means that we have created more of a competitive edge with our local activities, for example in Thailand," Lindahl said.
"As far as we stick to our hedging policy and protect our currencies, then it is just opportunities," he said.
